note: Outside the stated ICP on every commercial criterion, and the call confirmed it at two price points. Successful is a miss: he is a construction tradesman wearing a tool harness eight to ten hours a day, not a business owner or physician, and the business he mentions is a venture he is starting with his brother rather than an established one. Income is an unambiguous miss — he declined $6,000 and $4,000 and volunteered his own ceiling at 'a couple thousand', with capital committed to launching the new venture. Good-to-great is a miss: he is 195lb aiming for the high 170s, has not trained consistently for four or five months, and describes his own state as 'not to say that I'm in really bad physical health' but wanting to 'get a little bit better' — that is closer to rebuilding than to optimising. Two criteria do hold. Neglected health fits well: his body is the thing that has gone unattended while the physically punishing work continued, and he is not in crisis, being pain-free most of the time. Not-deconditioned also holds — he is physically active by occupation, not gym-averse, and about 20lb from his target rather than 50. The finding this call adds is that the funnel is not screening on the ICP at all: the prospect said the price was never disclosed on the application page and that the setter was vague about it, so a prospect whose budget was a fifth of the price consumed a full 50-minute closing slot.
